items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: Trumbauer had a band previously to this in St. Louis and he had PeeWee Russell and he had Bix and he had several other guys there too

ctx.x: Were you playing with the band?

No. Well, when he called me into to talk to me, he said -- I asked him, if he wanted me to play -- Do you want Horvath, the manager, if he wanted me to play. What did he want me to do with my horns? "Don't worry about it," but he says, "I'll tell you, why don't you do this. Saxophone players are a dime a dozen. I can get them. I can't get any arrangers." And he said, "We only have seven arrangements." Well, seven arrangements, I guess what he meant by that was of the top tunes of the day, because they played all…

those things along and a lot of them were memorized and a lot of them were put down like -- the Bix part would be written up, Trumbauer's part would be written up and then maybe some other part that they needed. The rhythm wouldn't be in there at all, so they had several of those things that they brought up and they played all -- a lot of Dixieland things that they later made records of with Trumbauer and with Bix, not with Goldkette.
